original_decisions.title: Compare the archive generated by Cargo publish dry-run
original_decisions.body:
A clean Cargo 1.97.1 publish dry-run writes the generated archive under target/package/tmp-crate. Compare that file against the same-run approved artifact before authentication. This changes one comparison path only; runtime, APIs, package inputs, lockfile, license/NOTICE and README are unchanged.

Validation: existing clean dry-run reproduces the missing old path and the corrected comparison passes; OSS policy, actionlint and zizmor pass. Exact approved tree: 695d26a6ad3e40408b218ed94680181fae1ad74f. No token values read or authentication permissions changed.

original_decisions.title: Prepare public crate distribution and standard Cargo release CI
original_decisions.body:
Prepares ihat-identity-assertion-contracts for public crates.io distribution with explicit package contents, release documentation, public dependency quality checks, and independently reviewed standard Cargo release CI. Runtime implementation, schemas, fixtures, Apache-2.0 license/NOTICE, and the original Cargo.lock remain unchanged.

Release prepare tests and verifies the actual crate without credentials. A separate gated publisher compares native no-verify repacking against the same run artifact before passing a token to standard Cargo. OIDC permissions cover the entire publish job. No registry tokens, environments or Trusted Publisher settings are configured by this PR.

Validation: exact independently accepted tree 9ff60b74ba196a422f460545471196fed6ff13a8; OSS policy, actionlint and zizmor passed. Identity tests 32, clippy and extracted-package compilation passed; current 62-file synthetic local archive SHA256 6b09486a6ccf2507c07ff32499913890d2e9bdd4b5cd5c6bcc95800a6bd0e559 matched native public-registry dry-run repacking. This local archive is not a hosted release approval.

original_decisions.title: Clarify usage, outcomes and implementation scope
original_decisions.body:
Readers can see what the repository enables, how to start, and which behavior is implemented. The README and usage guide retain declared dependency prerequisites and distinguish source verification from product or deployment acceptance.

Validation: local Markdown/link checks, source disclosure scan, unchanged license/notice, and existing OSS policy checks where defined. No package publication or deployment is requested.
